patterns.name: Directional Arrows on Links
patterns.description: Show directionality of relationships with arrow heads

code_example.code:
graph
  .linkDirectionalArrowLength(4)
  .linkDirectionalArrowColor(link => link.color || '#fff')
  .linkDirectionalArrowRelPos(0.5)  // 0=near source, 1=near target
  .linkDirectionalArrowResolution(8);

patterns.use_case: Dependency graphs, flow diagrams, hierarchical relationships

patterns.name: Directional Moving Particles
patterns.description: Animated particles flowing along links to indicate direction and flow

code_example.code:
graph
  .linkDirectionalParticles(4)
  .linkDirectionalParticleSpeed(0.02)  // fraction of link length per frame
  .linkDirectionalParticleWidth(0.8)
  .linkDirectionalParticleColor(link => link.color || '#00ffff')
  .linkDirectionalParticleOffset(0);   // initial position offset [0-1]

// For a single-shot particle effect:
graph.emitParticle(linkObject);

use_cases.code_snippet: graph.nodeThreeObject(n => DEVICE_GEOMETRIES[n.role]).nodePositionUpdate((obj, coords) => { obj.position.set(coords.x, coords.y, coords.z); return true; });

causes: link width is 0 with no source/target geometry
nodes are at exact same position
solutions: Verify source/target node IDs resolve correctly
Use linkLabel to verify links exist

causes: Using ngraph engine (no programmatic node access)

solutions: Use dagNodeFilter to exclude problematic nodes
Use onDagError to find and fix cycles in data
Always call graph._destructor() in useEffect cleanup
Check containerRef.current is not null before cleanup

troubleshooting.symptom: Poor performance with large graphs (10k+ nodes)
solutions: Use warmupTicks + cooldownTicks to pre-compute layout
Verify graph.nodeId() matches actual node ID field
Data may have source/target as objects instead of IDs

changes: Add controlType: 'orbit' option for smoother camera
3D introduces z-axis: consider nodePositionUpdate for planar data
nodeThreeObject accepts THREE.Object3D instead of Canvas 2D context
cameraPosition() takes {x, y, z} instead of {x, y}
React integration now uses react-force-graph package
All accessor functions now support function, string, and constant values uniformly
